hero.thesisTitle: OPtimisation EXplainability (OPEX) for Maintenance Scheduling in the Offshore Wind Industry
hero.summary: I combine multi-objective optimisation with explainable AI to produce offshore wind maintenance schedules that operators can understand and trust, and I study how uncertainty propagates through multi-agent Retrieval-Augmented Generation (RAG) pipelines that support those decisions.

pillars.label: Pillar 01 • Explainable Optimisation
pillars.title: OPEX: Optimisation Explainability in Offshore Wind Maintenance
pillars.body: Maintenance scheduling for offshore wind farms trades off cost against turbine availability. Evolutionary optimisers such as NSGA-II/III and MOPSO can find strong trade-offs, but operators need to understand why a schedule was chosen before they will act on it.
pillars.boxBody: The WOMBAT O&M simulator acts as the evaluation engine for NSGA-III, with SHAP-based explanations and agentic assistants that walk users through Pareto fronts and KPIs.

pillars.label: Pillar 02 • Agentic AI & UQ
pillars.title: Uncertainty Propagation in Multi-Agent RAG Pipelines
pillars.body: A Planner, Retriever, Evaluator and Generator agent each add their own uncertainty. If that uncertainty isn't tracked from stage to stage, a confident-sounding final answer can hide an unreliable chain of reasoning.
pillars.boxBody: Token-level and semantic entropy feed a latent uncertainty variable for each agent in a Bayesian network, which propagates it through the pipeline and decides whether to accept, flag or abstain.

publications.title: Bayesian Uncertainty Propagation for Agentic RAG Pipelines: A Proof-of-Concept Study on Multi-Hop Question Answering
publications.summary: A Bayesian network that tracks uncertainty as it moves through a four-agent RAG pipeline. Token-level and semantic entropy from each agent feed a per-agent latent uncertainty node, so the system can tell when a multi-hop answer should be accepted, flagged for review, or withheld.

highlights.label: Pipeline stages
highlights.detail: Planner, Retriever, Evaluator and Generator, each with its own uncertainty node.

highlights.label: Entropy inputs
highlights.detail: Token-level entropy and semantic entropy enter the network as separate evidence.

highlights.label: Decision policy
highlights.detail: Accept, flag or abstain, depending on the propagated uncertainty.

publications.title: Stage-Wise Uncertainty Scores in Agentic RAG: An Exploratory Study of Deterministic Failure-OR Fusion
publications.bibtexVenue: 7th International Conference on Maintenance and Intelligent Asset Management (ICMIAM 2026)
publications.summary: Explores scoring uncertainty separately at each stage of an agentic RAG pipeline and fusing the scores deterministically with failure-OR logic. Presented at the 7th International Conference on Maintenance and Intelligent Asset Management, 2 September 2026.

publications.title: When Can Operators Trust an AI Explanation? Runtime Monitoring of Agentic Pipelines in Offshore Wind
publications.summary: A three-layer architecture: an NSGA-III maintenance optimiser, a four-agent RAG pipeline that explains and challenges its schedules, and a Bayesian uncertainty monitor that decides when the system's recommendations can be trusted.
